editorial.headline: Government Libraries: A Public-Service Activity Closed to Foreign Capital
editorial.standfirst: Government library work spans collections, access and preservation—yet it is closed to foreign investment nationally and for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this government-library activity in Bali today. The national position is equally clear: its PMA status is **TERTUTUP**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. This is therefore a public-service activity with no foreign-equity route under the record’s national classification.

The work itself is broader than shelving books. It covers the management, care, preservation and appraisal of libraries operated by government institutions. That includes documentation and information services across government libraries, including digital libraries, reading rooms, listening rooms and viewing rooms. It also reaches the organisation and cataloguing of collections, alongside lending and storage of books, maps, periodicals, films, recordings, tapes and artworks.

Its defining setting is institutional. The operators identified are government bodies at national, regional and local level, provided the library is not under an educational institution or another cultural institution. The activity also includes retrieving library documents to meet information needs. No business scales are listed as open in the record, reinforcing that this classification should be read through its stated public-government function rather than as a general commercial library-services category.

Bali’s record also marks the activity **TERTUTUP** and blocked for PMA registration. Its stated reason places the activity at medium-high or high risk and says it is not blocked by Bali’s island-wide moratorium; the relevant position must instead be verified for the address concerned. That distinction matters: the moratorium applies to all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities, but it is not the stated basis here. It does not change the practical conclusion for foreign investment: the activity remains closed nationally and closed for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The moratorium is not the stated basis in Bali, but the practical conclusion remains the same: this activity is closed to foreign investment.
